Engineering Interview Templates: Minimal Cheatsheets for DSA, LLD, and HLD

Nov 11, 2026Engineering Practices
#interviews#system-design#low-level-design#dsa#architecture

A collection of minimal, copy-pasteable interview checklists and structured response templates for Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA), Low-Level Design (LLD), and High-Level System Design (HLD).

1. Coding / DSA Round Template

Target Time: 45 minutes (Clarify: 5m | Approach & Trade-offs: 10m | Code: 20m | Test & Dry Run: 7m | Wrap-up: 3m)

Step 1: Clarification & Bounds

  • Inputs & Outputs: Types, bounds, return format, empty/null handling.
  • Constraints: Can items be negative? Are there duplicates? Is input sorted? Can we mutate in-place?
  • Constraint $\to$ Expected Complexity Guide:
    • $N \le 10 \implies O(N!)$ (Backtracking)
    • $N \le 20 \implies O(2^N)$ (Bitmask / Subsets)
    • $N \le 500 \implies O(N^3)$ (Floyd-Warshall, 3D DP)
    • $N \le 5 \times 10^3 \implies O(N^2)$ (Nested loops, 2D DP)
    • $N \le 10^5 \implies O(N \log N)$ (Sorting, Divide & Conquer, Binary Search)
    • $N \le 10^7 \implies O(N)$ (Two Pointers, Sliding Window, Monotonic Stack, Hash Map)
    • $N \ge 10^9 \implies O(\log N)$ or $O(1)$ (Binary Search on Answer, Math)

Step 2: Test Cases to State Upfront

  1. Standard Case: Normal, non-trivial input.
  2. Edge Cases: Empty array, single element, all duplicates, negative values.
  3. Adversarial Case: Inverted order, extreme bounds, large skew.

Step 3: Pattern Identification

  • Two Pointers: Sorted arrays, pairs, opposite ends, merging.
  • Sliding Window: Subarrays or substrings with dynamic/fixed length constraint $K$.
  • Fast & Slow Pointers: Cycle detection, finding list middle.
  • Monotonic Stack / Queue: Next greater/smaller element, range bounds, sliding window max.
  • Binary Search on Answer: Monotonic feasibility function (isPossible(mid)).
  • BFS / DFS: Shortest path in unweighted graphs (BFS), tree traversals, connected components (DFS).
  • Topological Sort: Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAG), build order, task dependencies.
  • Union-Find (DSU): Dynamic connectivity, cycle check in undirected graphs.
  • Dynamic Programming: Overlapping subproblems, state definition & transitions.

Step 4: Implementation Checklist

  • [ ] Guard clauses for null, empty, or out-of-range inputs first.
  • [ ] Descriptive variable names (leftIndex, currentSum instead of i, s).
  • [ ] Explicit loop invariants and state updates.
  • [ ] Modular helpers if logic exceeds 15–20 lines.

Step 5: Dry-Run & Complexity

  • [ ] Trace an edge case line-by-line using a variable state table.
  • [ ] State Time Complexity: Average and worst-case with justification.
  • [ ] State Space Complexity: Distinguish auxiliary memory from output memory.

2. Low-Level Design (LLD / Machine Coding) Template

Target Time: 45–60 minutes (Scope: 8m | Entities & Relationships: 12m | Patterns: 10m | Coding: 25m | Review: 5m)

📚 Related Design Pattern Deep Dives:

  • Design Patterns: Architectural Overview & SOLID Principles
  • Creational Patterns Guide (Factories, Builder, Singleton, Prototype)
  • Structural Patterns & The "Wrapper Family" (Decorator, Proxy, Facade, Adapter, Composite, Flyweight, Bridge)
  • Behavioral Patterns Guide (Strategy, Observer, Command, Chain of Responsibility, Mediator, State)

Step 1: Requirements & Scope Bounding

  • In-Scope (Must Have): 2–3 core functional workflows.
  • Out-of-Scope (Won't Have): External gateways, auth services, persistence UI.
  • Non-Functional Focus: Thread safety, extensibility, testability.

Step 2: Domain Modeling Checklist

  1. Nouns $\to$ Entities / Classes: Identify primary domain actors and models.
  2. Verbs $\to$ Behaviors / Methods: Place business logic where state lives (Information Expert).
  3. Relationships:
    • Inheritance (is-a): Use strictly for polymorphic behavior.
    • Composition (has-a): Prefer over inheritance for flexibility.
    • Dependency (uses-a): Method parameters and injected dependencies.
  4. Value Objects & Enums: Avoid primitive obsession; use enums for statuses and types.

Step 3: Pattern Selection Matrix

Scenario / NeedDesign PatternLink to Pattern Deep Dive
Swappable algorithms / dynamic pricing / sorting policiesStrategyStrategy Pattern
Event alerts, dashboard updates, listenersObserverObserver Pattern
Multi-type object creation decoupled from clientsFactory MethodFactory Method
Multi-level part-whole hierarchies (groups, trees)CompositeComposite Pattern
Dynamic add-ons, decorators, wrappersDecoratorDecorator Pattern
Complex state transitions without switch blocksStateState Pattern
Auditable operations, undo/redo, task queuesCommandCommand Pattern
Coordinating complex workflows across colleaguesMediatorMediator Pattern

Step 4: Concurrency & Defensive Coding Checklist

  • [ ] Critical state updates protected (ReentrantLock, synchronized, or atomic primitives).
  • [ ] Thread-safe collections used where needed (ConcurrentHashMap, CopyOnWriteArrayList).
  • [ ] Immutability enforced for identifiers and timestamps (final / readonly).
  • [ ] Validations with descriptive exceptions (IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException).

Step 5: Minimal Code Organization Structure

src/
├── model/       # Pure domain entities, value objects, enums
├── strategy/    # Interfaces and swappable algorithm implementations
├── repository/  # In-memory storage abstraction (Map-backed)
├── service/     # Stateful coordinator / business logic service
└── Main.java    # Driver demonstration covering all requirements & edge cases

3. High-Level Design (HLD / System Design) Template

Use this exact structure during system design interviews:

1. Requirements & System Clarifications
   ├── Functional Requirements
   └── Non-Functional Requirements
2. Capacity Estimations & Scale Profile
3. API Design
4. High-Level Analysis
5. High-Level Architecture
   ├── Core Solution
   └── Infra Diagram
6. Detailed Component Deep Dives
7. Edge Cases & Operational Resilience
8. Failure Modes & Mitigations
9. Misc (Scaling, Security, Compliance, Telemetry)

1. Requirements & System Clarifications

Functional Requirements (FR)

  • Define 3–4 explicit user actions/journeys.
  • Clarify data inputs and expected return formats.
  • Explicitly state what is out of scope (e.g. billing, user profile management).

Non-Functional Requirements (NFR)

  • Availability vs. Consistency (CAP): AP (high availability, eventual consistency) vs. CP (strong consistency).
  • Latency SLAs: p99 read $< 20\text{ms}$; p99 write $< 100\text{ms}$.
  • Throughput Target: Daily Active Users (DAU), peak traffic multiplier ($2\times$–$5\times$).
  • Durability: Zero data loss for committed writes (multi-zone replication).

2. Capacity Estimations & Scale Profile

Math Shortcuts:
• 1 Day ≈ 10^5 seconds (86,400)
• 1M requests/day ≈ 10 requests/sec (QPS)
• 100M requests/day ≈ 1,000 QPS
• 80/20 Rule: 20% of content drives 80% of read traffic (cache sizing)
MetricEstimation FormulaNotes
Write QPS$\frac{\text{DAU} \times \text{writes per user}}{10^5\text{ s}}$Peak = $2\times$ to $3\times$ Average
Read QPS$\text{Write QPS} \times \text{Read-to-Write Ratio}$E.g. $10:1$ or $100:1$
Storage / Day$\text{Daily Writes} \times \text{Payload Size}$Multiply by $365 \times Y$ years $\times 1.3$ (indexes)
Cache Memory$\text{Daily Reads} \times 0.20 \times \text{Payload Size}$Sized for 20% hot working set
Network Bandwidth$\text{QPS} \times \text{Payload Size} \times 8$Separate into Ingress (writes) and Egress (reads)

3. API Design

Define explicit endpoint signatures, HTTP methods, headers, and payloads:

POST /api/v1/{resource}
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
  Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
Body: { "field": "value" }
Response: 201 Created -> { "id": "...", "status": "PENDING" }

GET /api/v1/{resource}/{id}
Response: 200 OK -> { "id": "...", "data": "..." }

GET /api/v1/{resource}?cursor=<token>&limit=20
Response: 200 OK -> { "items": [...], "next_cursor": "<token>" }
  • HTTP Verbs: POST (create), GET (read), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE.
  • Idempotency: Include Idempotency-Key headers for write operations.
  • Pagination: Use keyset/cursor pagination over offset pagination for large tables.

4. High-Level Analysis

Address core architectural trade-offs before diagramming:

  • Communication Model: Synchronous (HTTP/gRPC) vs. Asynchronous (Kafka / SQS / Event Bus).
  • Delivery Guarantees: At-least-once with idempotent consumers vs. Exactly-once.
  • Database Choice:
    • Relational (PostgreSQL/MySQL): ACID transactions, complex joins, structured schemas.
    • NoSQL Key-Value/Document (DynamoDB, Cassandra): Massive horizontal write scale, simple key lookups, zero joins.
    • Search/Time-Series (OpenSearch, ClickHouse): Full-text queries, log analysis, time-series aggregations.

5. High-Level Architecture

Core Solution

  1. Client hits DNS $\to$ routed to closest Edge CDN/WAF.
  2. API Gateway / L7 Load Balancer handles SSL termination, auth, and rate limiting.
  3. Stateless Services process business logic, reading from/writing to cache and database.
  4. Message Broker decouples long-running or async downstream workloads.

Infra Diagram

[ Client (Web/Mobile) ]
          │ HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
          ▼
   [ DNS / Route 53 ]
          │
          ▼
   [ CDN / WAF Edge ]
          │
          ▼
[ Load Balancer / API Gateway ]
          │
   ┌──────┴──────────────────────────┐
   │ (Stateless App Services)        │
   │ [Service Pod]     [Service Pod] │
   └──────┬──────────────────┬───────┘
          │                  │
    (Cache-Aside)            │ (Async Event)
          ▼                  ▼
  [ Redis Cluster ]    [ Message Queue (Kafka/SQS) ]
          │                  │
    (Fallback)               ▼
          ▼            [ Async Consumer Workers ]
[ Primary DB (Write) ]       │
   │                         ▼
   ├──► [ Read Replica ] ──► [ Search / Analytics Store ]
   └──► [ Read Replica ]

6. Detailed Component Deep Dives

Pick the 2–3 biggest bottlenecks in the system:

  • Unique ID Generation: Snowflake ID (Timestamp + Node ID + Sequence) vs. UUIDv4 vs. DB Auto-increment with ticket servers.
  • Partitioning / Sharding Strategy: Hash-based partitioning via Consistent Hashing ring with virtual nodes to avoid hotspots.
  • Read-After-Write Consistency: Route immediate reads for recently written records to the primary database or local cache.
  • Cache Strategy: Cache-aside vs. Write-through; TTL policies; eviction policy (LRU / LFU).

7. Edge Cases & Operational Resilience

  • Cache Stampede / Thundering Herd: Use distributed locks (Redis Redlock) or probabilistic early expiration (XFetch).
  • Hot Partition / Celebrity Problem: Add local in-process cache (Caffeine) on app servers or salt partition keys (key_prefix_randomInt).
  • Concurrent Writes & Race Conditions: Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) using version numbers, or distributed pessimistic locks.
  • Backpressure: Bounded queues, client retry policies with exponential backoff and full jitter.

8. Failure Modes & Mitigations

Failure ModeImpactMitigation Strategy
Cache Node DownSpike in database read queriesCircuit breaker trips; serve stale data; fallback to in-memory app cache.
Primary Database DownWrite operations failAutomated failover via consensus (Raft/Paxos); promote read replica.
Message Queue LagDelayed asynchronous processingAuto-scale consumer group workers; provision disk-buffered topic partitions.
Network Partition (Split-Brain)Inconsistent writes across zonesQuorum-based writes ($W + R > N$); fence off minority partitions.
Downstream Service OutageCascading thread starvationCircuit breakers (Resilience4j) with fallback responses; bounded thread pools.

9. Misc

Scaling

  • Stateless Tier: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) driven by CPU/Memory or queue depth.
  • Database Tier: Read replicas for read scaling; sharding on entity ID for write scaling.

Security

  • Auth: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect with short-lived JWTs.
  • Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest (AWS KMS).
  • Perimeter: WAF rate limiting (Token Bucket) per IP and API key; DDoS protection.

Compliance

  • GDPR / CCPA: Soft-delete flags with automated background purges; anonymize PII; data export pipelines.
  • Audit Trails: Immutable, append-only logs for all sensitive administrative actions.

Telemetry (Observability)

  • Metrics:
    • RED Method (Services): Rate (QPS), Errors (4xx/5xx), Duration (p50/p95/p99 latency).
    • USE Method (Infra): Utilization, Saturation, Errors (CPU, memory, disk, network).
  • Tracing: OpenTelemetry distributed tracing headers (traceparent) across microservices.
  • Logs: Centralized JSON structured logs (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch).
  • Alerts: PagerDuty triggers on SLA breaches (e.g. $p99 > 100\text{ms}$ or error rate $> 1%$).
